item.text:
<linkedin_post>Sharing scientific data publicly is only one part of making it available for reuse. A researcher also needs to know where the data came from, what it contains and how to work with it. A file in a legacy format with little documentation can be difficult to use even when anyone can download it.

Project ProtoStar is bringing research institutions and open science organizations together to encourage the release of suitable datasets, models and code in machine-actionable formats. Its partners include universities working through the Open Forum for AI, the Astera Institute, Hugging Face and the Open Research Community Accelerator.

The project will use open challenges to see what people can build with these resources and to identify obstacles they encounter along the way. Carnegie Mellon University hosts the first challenge, focused on urban climate forecasting, from November 2–13.</linkedin_post>
